issue.title: Decide and pin the alias-pool counterpart to the tier-mapping advisory guard
issue.description:
Follow-up from plan `202609/muse_contributor_size_aliases.md`.

`tests/llm_provider/test_model_advisories.py::test_tier_mapping_never_routes_to_an_advisory_model`
guards one of the two automatic routes to an advisory-flagged model: a provider's tier
map. The other route — membership in a shipped size-alias pool in
`src/sase/llm_provider/model_alias_defaults.yml` — has no counterpart. After that plan
lands, `@xsmall`, `@small`, and `@medium` deliberately include
`muse/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` (Meta trains on its inputs and outputs), and nothing in
the test suite or any decision record says whether that was an allowed exception, a
one-off, or the new norm. The asymmetry exists by accident, not by decision.

Related: `sase-14e` (the doctor check only sees the selected pool member).

task_type_fields.proposal:
Decide, then record and enforce, the rule for advisory-flagged models in shipped alias
pools. The credible options are: (a) an explicit allowlist test that names each
advisory-flagged model permitted in a shipped pool, so adding one is a reviewed, visible
edit; (b) a required acknowledgement field in the pool entry that the loader and a test
insist on; or (c) an explicit decision that there is no rule, written down so the
asymmetry with the tier-map guard is deliberate. Whichever is chosen should land as a
test (a, b) and/or an immutable decision record (all three).
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
The plan that surfaced this was scoped to adding the Muse member to the three pools, and
its own text tells the implementer not to soften the change or widen it. Choosing an
allowlist-versus-acknowledgement-versus-nothing policy is a project-level decision (and,
if it lands as a decision record, a memory change), not part of a docs/YAML/tests edit.
